en.title: Delete the Fewest Elements So That at Most One More Deletion Makes the Array Increasing
en.description:
The array elements are distinct. An array is called almost increasing if and only if deleting at most one more element makes it strictly increasing. Find the minimum number of elements to delete from the given array so that the remaining array is almost increasing. The original text mistakenly joined [13] and [9,2] into [13,9,2] and called it valid; this is corrected according to the full definition and the identical problem 29: three decreasing items are not almost increasing.

The ranges added by this site for missing bounds and the recovery of source typos are described in the input protocol.
en.input: The input gives n and n distinct integers. The original gives no numeric bounds; this site adds 1≤n≤100000, −10^9≤a[i]≤10^9.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 1; 1; 0. They have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Find the length L of the longest strictly increasing subsequence; the answer is max(0,n−L−1).
